name: The Dicks
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: Floyd's band began as fake flyers, played its first real show with a purple mohawk on stage, and ended up covered by Mudhoney and the Jesus Lizard.

eras.title: A poster band gets real
eras.text: Gary Floyd, a gay communist in a city that had never asked for one, invents a band on paper and then has to staff it. Within weeks it is playing the first all-local punk bill at the Armadillo and cutting a single with a title that says the whole thing.

years.src: Austin Chronicle: Gary Floyd has died · KUTX: Remembering Gary Floyd · Razorcake · Lansing City Pulse
years.h: Gary Floyd papers Austin with flyers for a band that doesn't exist
years.p: The Dicks began as a prank: posters for fake shows and bogus line-ups. Then somebody offered a real gig, and Floyd found a bassist, a drummer and a guitarist.
years.xp:
Floyd had grown up in Palestine, Texas, spent two years in Houston as a conscientious objector working as a janitor at a state hospital, and moved to Austin in 1974, according to the Austin Chronicle. The fake-band flyers went up around town announcing shows and line-ups that didn't exist (KUTX), and Floyd later met [[Buxf Parrott|fd008890-d1a5-4e38-afcb-19cd617ebb93]] and [[Glen Taylor|3fcfca8e-496f-4cce-b93e-9e4fe1106d46]], who became the real thing (Razorcake). [[Pat Deason|38bb97e6-0c28-4942-be7c-acbd239a9322]] completed the four.

Floyd, on the pitch: “We also said we were communists, we were drag queens.”

years.cap: The Punk Prom bill. Photo needed.
years.src: KUTX: Punk Prom · Texas State Historical Association
years.h: Punk Prom: the Dicks play their first show at the Armadillo
years.p: Big Boys, the Next, the Reactors, Sharon Tate's Baby and the Dicks made up the first all-local punk bill at the Armadillo World Headquarters. Floyd wore a purple and pink mohawk.
years.xp:
It was the Armadillo's last year, and the room that had hosted Austin's hippie and country royalty gave a night to teenagers with shaved heads. The Dicks had been a band for only weeks (KUTX).

Floyd on Austin punk: “It had nothing to do with the Sex Pistols or the Ramones. It had to do with your own personal life changing.” The TSHA Handbook lists this as the band's debut.

years.src: Razorcake · Wikipedia: The Dicks Hate the Police · Xtra Magazine
years.h: The Dicks Hate the Police 7-inch on MDC's R Radical label
years.p: Three songs: the title track, "Lifetime Problems" and "All Night Fever". Dave Dictor of [[MDC|0f3c4d10-e541-46f0-a589-61ad701c6ce4]] ran the label.
years.xp:
Razorcake's interview with Floyd credits Taylor with writing much of the title track. Wikipedia collects the verdicts: Pitchfork on the state power it describes, and the Dallas Observer calling it perhaps the finest single ever released by a Texas punk band.

Mudhoney would pick it up a decade later.

years.src: Texas State Historical Association · BrooklynVegan: The Dicks From Texas · Wikipedia: Live at Raul's Club
years.h: Live at Raul's Club: half a split LP with the Big Boys
years.p: Ten Dicks songs, including "Fake Bands", "Wheelchair Epidemic" and "Dead in a Motel Room", recorded live at Raul's on September 19 and 20.
years.xp: In the Dicks From Texas documentary, [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]] says the split got heavy rotation at the SST offices, and [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] recalls a show where the Dicks opened for Minor Threat (BrooklynVegan). Selfless Records later put six songs from it on a double 7-inch in 1992 (Wikipedia).

eras.title: Liver, frosting, and a bus to California
eras.text: Raul's is home base, Floyd's stage act involves the contents of his underwear, and the rest of the country starts to hear about it. Then Floyd leaves.

years.src: KUTX: Remembering Gary Floyd · Houston Press · Xtra Magazine · Lansing City Pulse
years.h: Raul's is home, and Floyd's panties are the prop closet
years.p: For about three years the club was the base. Floyd pulled frosting and liver out of his panties to throw at the crowd.
years.xp:
The Houston Press describes Floyd in drag, tossing squirty condoms and using his large body "as a symbol of defiance." Floyd, decades on: “shoving liver in my panties to throw on people, though I'd use vegan liver now.”

Xtra reports a 1981 photo of Floyd and the Big Boys' Randy "Biscuit" Turner, both in drag, that ran on a magazine cover. Turner was also out.

years.src: Alternative Tentacles: Dicks · Texas State Historical Association · Trouser Press · Wikipedia: Dicks (band)
years.h: Floyd moves to San Francisco, and the Dicks stop being one band
years.p: Alternative Tentacles and the Texas State Historical Association both put the move in 1982; Floyd went with manager Debbie Gordon.
years.xp: Sources split on the year: TSHA has October 1982, while Wikipedia and several obituaries say 1983. Trouser Press says most of the band went back to Austin while Floyd stayed in California.

eras.title: Kill from the Heart
eras.text: The Texas line-up makes its best-known record for SST, then hits the road on a three-month Rock Against Reagan tour. In San Francisco the band gets rebuilt.

years.src: Austin Chronicle: Dicks reissues · Wikipedia: Kill from the Heart
years.h: Kill from the Heart: the Texas Dicks' last record, on SST
years.p: Spot produced it. Tim Kerr of the Big Boys played dobro on one track and the Torn Panties sang on "Anti-Klan (Part Two)".
years.xp:
The Austin Chronicle called it "a dozen two-minute grenades" aimed at Austin's status quo, with "raw minimalism cut with in-studio exclamations." It includes a Jimi Hendrix cover (Wikipedia), and it was the last recording by the original four.

[[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]] remastered it for Alternative Tentacles in 2012, with the three-track Hate the Police single as bonus.

years.h: Three months on the Rock Against Reagan tour
years.p: The Dicks joined the political hardcore package tour, per the Texas State Historical Association and Alternative Tentacles.

years.src: Wikipedia: These People · Razorcake · Wikipedia: Dicks (band)
years.h: A San Francisco Dicks: Tim Carroll, Sebastian Fuchs, Lynn Perko
years.p: Carroll on guitar, Fuchs on bass and Lynn Perko, formerly of the Wrecks, on drums replace the Texans. Debbie Gordon manages.
years.xp: Gordon is credited as "mood coordinator" on These People. In the Razorcake interview Floyd calls Perko crucial to the San Francisco band's sound.

eras.title: Blues, and the exit
eras.text: The San Francisco Dicks slow down and get bluesier, sign with the label of the Dead Kennedys' singer and get one record out before Floyd closes the book.

years.h: Peace? 7-inch, back on R Radical
years.p: The same year the band gave "I Hope You Get Drafted" to R Radical's International P.E.A.C.E. benefit compilation.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dicks (band) · Austin Chronicle: Gary Floyd has died
years.h: The Butthole Surfers write a song called "Gary Floyd"
years.p: The Austin noise band put a tribute to the singer on record in 1984.
years.xp: Drummer [[King Coffey|f275d56b-3601-476f-a4bf-b50892750984]] told the story of his "first major rock & roll epiphany": a Dicks show in Fort Worth (Austin Chronicle).

years.src: Alternative Tentacles: Dicks · Austin Chronicle: Dicks reissues · Wikipedia: These People
years.h: These People: the San Francisco Dicks on Alternative Tentacles
years.p: Klaus Flouride of the Dead Kennedys produced twelve songs, among them "Off-Duty Sailor", "The Police (Force)" and "George Jackson".
years.xp: Alternative Tentacles says the band had moved toward longer, blues-rock songs by now. The Austin Chronicle's 2012 verdict was that a sonic upgrade "can't compensate for the debut's pissed-off and sweaty Austin shack aesthetic."

years.big: “A 300-pound communist drag queen who can sing like Janis Joplin.”
years.src: KQED: Gary Floyd · BrooklynVegan: Gary Floyd
years.h: What Jello Biafra saw in Gary Floyd
years.p: That is Biafra's description of Floyd, as KQED reported it. His label released These People.
years.xp: David Yow of the Jesus Lizard put it another way after Floyd's death: “It was like Diana Ross meets Johnny Rotten.” (BrooklynVegan)

years.h: Floyd ends the Dicks and starts Sister Double Happiness
years.p: He and Perko carry on in San Francisco with a new band.
years.xp: In Razorcake's interview Floyd talks about the San Francisco scene turning more male and pit-heavy, which made it harder for women to take part. He wanted to go in other directions.

eras.title: The songs go to Seattle
eras.text: Floyd tours with Nirvana and Soundgarden as Sister Double Happiness while Mudhoney and the Jesus Lizard keep the old Dicks songs alive. The band's guitarist dies in 1997.

years.src: Trouser Press · CVLT Nation · Xtra Magazine · Stereogum
years.h: Sister Double Happiness: SST, Reprise, Sub Pop
years.p: Floyd and Perko's blues-rock band records for SST (1988), Reprise (Heart and Mind, 1991) and Sub Pop (Horsey Water, 1994).
years.xp: Floyd says the band toured with Nirvana around Nevermind and with Soundgarden around Badmotorfinger (CVLT Nation, Xtra). Stereogum has it active until 1995.

years.src: Austin Chronicle: Dicks reissues · Wikipedia: The Dicks Hate the Police · Stereogum
years.h: Mudhoney cover "Hate the Police" and a new crowd hears it
years.p: The Seattle band's version is on Superfuzz Bigmuff Plus Early Singles.
years.xp: The Austin Chronicle says the song was "famously preserved during intervening decades by Mudhoney". Wikipedia and Stereogum add that the [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]] covered "Wheelchair Epidemic".

years.src: KQED: The Dicks final show · Texas State Historical Association · Wikipedia: Dicks (band)
years.h: Glen Taylor dies, and Alternative Tentacles issues 1980–1986
years.p: The guitarist died of liver and kidney failure, according to KQED. The compilation came out the same year.
years.xp: The TSHA Handbook describes his playing as "a dazzling combination of simultaneous rhythm and lead chords not unlike Jimi Hendrix." It also notes that he and Floyd were both openly gay.

eras.title: Home for the last shows
eras.text: Floyd, Parrott and Deason get back together, a documentary takes sixteen years to finish and a tribute album gathers 27 bands. The last shows are at home.

years.src: KQED: The Dicks final show · Xtra Magazine · Wikipedia: Dicks (band)
years.h: Floyd, Parrott and Deason reunite, with new guitarists
years.p: Mark Kenyon, Brian Magee and later Davy Jones take the guitar seat.
years.xp: Floyd, on the reunion: “It was a little rough for a while, but we were always close. They're my brothers.” (KQED) Xtra places a 2004 reunion show at Eagle's Tavern in San Francisco; Wikipedia says regular concerts in Austin followed. The Dicks went into the Austin Music Awards' Texas Music Hall of Fame in 2009.

years.src: Houston Press · BrooklynVegan: The Dicks From Texas · Wikipedia: Dicks (band)
years.h: The Dicks From Texas: a documentary and a 27-band tribute
years.p: Cindy Marabito's film took 16 years to make; the tribute album has 27 bands covering 28 songs.
years.xp: Rollins, MacKaye, Yow and [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]] appear in the film (Houston Press). Davy Jones, the reunion band's guitarist since 2005, died in 2015 (Wikipedia). The film was released in February 2016, per BrooklynVegan.

yt: Hate the Police, Grizzly Hall, Oct 31 2016
years.h: The last Dicks shows, at Grizzly Hall in Austin
years.p: Floyd chose Austin for the finale, to thank the city for a benefit held there in 2013.
years.xp: Floyd told KQED the benefit was held when he faced housing difficulties, and that he had never been able to go back on stage there and say thanks. “I've never been able to go on stage there since then and say 'thank you.'”

years.src: Austin Chronicle: Gary Floyd has died · BrooklynVegan: Gary Floyd · Stereogum · KQED: Gary Floyd
years.h: Gary Floyd dies at 71
years.p: He died of congestive heart failure, according to the Austin Chronicle and BrooklynVegan; he was survived by his husband.
years.xp: Mike Watt announced it on Facebook (Stereogum). Floyd had published the memoir Please Bee Nice: My Life up 'til Now (2014) and the lyric book I Said That (2017), and shown paintings in 2022 (KQED). Some reports give May 2 and others May 3.
